problem: Existing VLN agents optimise geometric reachability and ignore semantic regulatory constraints (e.g. 'No Entry' signs). They fall into a 'Goal-driven trap', and no benchmark tests rule-compliant urban navigation.
motivation: Real-world deployment requires social compliance and safety, not just reaching the goal. Small-footprint traffic signs are overridden by salient geometric priors in current models, and retraining is costly and hurts overall navigation performance. This motivates a benchmark plus a plug-and-play, training-free rectification module.
key_idea: Inject realistic traffic-rule signs into the Touchdown graph to build Rule-VLN, and add a zero-shot module (SNRM) that detects signs with coarse-to-fine VLM perception and replans detours with an epistemic mental map.
insight: Both perception and recovery are needed. Removing macro-micro prompting or rule grounding raises Level-4 CVR from 23.68 to 26.86 or 25.94. Removing the mental map gives the lowest CVR (21.28) but TC drops to 6.53, because the agent stops at constraints without a detour. Visual-spatial grounding matters more than VLM size: Pixtral-12B underperforms the 8B models, and LLaVA is over-conservative.
method: Rule-VLN task formulation: a binary validity mask over edges, decided by whether the visual slice contains a prohibition from rule set R, yields a semantically pruned graph; the agent must find a compliant detour.

CityNav-Rules-73K: 73,937 samples across 177 categories; GPT-5 maps each category to a permissible action subspace (Straight/Left/Right/U-turn); a hybrid of visual descriptors and semantic imperatives.

Node selection and curriculum: a criticality score combines degree centrality, betweenness centrality, path dependence and path frequency; 8,180 nodes are split into four levels, with affected instructions rising from 31.44% to 91.13%.

MPSI: a road-mask-anchored, dual-mask-conditioned DiT (Insert Anything style) with CLIP reference features synthesises signs into panorama crops; a GMM (K=2) over CLIP alignment scores filters low-quality outputs before stitching back.

SNRM dual-stage perception: DINO detects candidate cues; a macro (boxed global view) plus micro (magnified crop) visual prompt is built; SigLIP retrieves the top rule text from a knowledge base (KDRG); a VLM (Qwen3-VL) with CoT outputs Safe or a corrected action, gating the base policy's action.

Epistemic mental map: a local 2D virtual topology with dead-reckoned position; a penalised greedy heuristic picks the candidate closest to the virtual target and penalises backtracking; a visual memory buffer with cosine similarity detects loops and forces a detour.
CVR metric: violations normalised by the agent's exposure to nodes near active constraints.

setting.backbone: Frozen base VLN policies (Loc4Plan, FLAME) + SNRM using Qwen3-VL-8B (zero-shot), DINO detector, SigLIP retrieval
setting.model_size: 8B (Qwen3-VL); 4B, LLaVA-7B, InternVL-8B and Pixtral-12B also tested
setting.training_data: none for SNRM (training-free); base models trained on Rule-VLN, and FLAME re-fine-tuned with FOV widened from 60° to 120°; the MPSI dataset is CityNav-Rules-73K
setting.observation: Street-view panoramas (Touchdown), sliced into views, with injected signs
setting.action_space: Discrete Touchdown graph actions (straight, left, right, U-turn / stop)
setting.simulator: Touchdown street-view graph (29k nodes) with synthesised sign images

numbers.eval_set_note: Level-1; the paper does not name the split
numbers.extra: SNRM is training-free; FLAME retrained with 120° FOV

numbers_note: The paper does not name a split for Rule-VLN, so 'test' is assumed. Levels 1-4 are treated as separate rows. The baseline performance figure was not available as numbers, only the FLAME/Loc4Plan columns in the table. Loc4Plan Level-1/3/4 rows omitted for brevity.
results: SNRM lowers CVR and raises TC when added to FLAME and Loc4Plan. On FLAME Level-3, CVR drops by 19.26 (41.79 to 22.53) and TC rises by 5.97 (11.43 to 17.40). Gains shrink at Level-4 (TC 8.95 to 9.94). MPSI beats FLUX.1-Fill on synthesis quality (PSNR 32.41 vs 24.59, FID 7.72 vs 30.31) with 58.81% less VRAM.
limitations: Absolute TC stays low (9.94 at Level-4; 17.40 at Level-3), and CVR is still above 20% for the best model.
Injected signs are synthetic images on a single Touchdown city graph, and there is no real-robot evaluation.
SNRM depends on a fixed rule knowledge base and a large VLM, and a preemptive detour can cost TC, as in the no-map ablation.
